children: Integrated offering combines Nota Vision Agent with the Intel Arc Pro B70 GPU, reducing the need for customers to select hardware and perform separate optimization work
A single Intel Arc Pro B70 GPU processes 32 video channels simultaneously at a combined rate of 540 frames per second, exceeding the performance target set for real-world operations
Nota AI and Intel plan to expand their collaboration through joint customer development, deployment consulting and on-site technical support

SEOUL, South Korea, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nota AI, a company specializing in AI model compression and optimization, today announced the launch of an integrated solution combining its AI video monitoring solution, Nota Vision Agent (NVA), with the Intel® Arc™ Pro B70 graphics processing unit (GPU).

The commercial bundle pairs the Intel Arc Pro B70 GPU with NVA software optimized for the GPU's compute architecture. By providing the hardware and optimized software as an integrated offering, the solution reduces the need for customers to select hardware and perform separate optimization work. The product is available for purchase through Nota AI, which also provides deployment consultation.

The Intel Arc Pro B70 is designed for professional graphics and AI workloads. Combined with Nota AI's optimization technology, it enables organizations to deploy vision-language model (VLM)-based video monitoring systems tailored to their performance requirements, available budgets and existing infrastructure.

Demand for AI-powered video monitoring is growing across intelligent transportation systems (ITS), industrial safety and selective video monitoring. However, organizations often operate under different conditions, including the number of CCTV channels, required processing performance, available budgets and existing infrastructure. This can make it challenging to select and optimize the appropriate hardware and software for each deployment.

To address these challenges, Nota AI optimized NVA for the Intel Arc Pro B70 architecture, while Intel provided technical support for the hardware and software environment. The resulting solution allows customers to deploy a VLM-based video monitoring system without undertaking separate hardware selection and optimization processes, helping reduce deployment complexity and improve operational efficiency.

In performance testing, a single Intel Arc Pro B70 GPU processed 32 video channels simultaneously at a combined rate of 540 frames per second (FPS), averaging 16.9 FPS per channel. The result exceeded the 15 FPS target established for the ITS operating environment, demonstrating that the solution can maintain the processing speed required to analyze multiple CCTV feeds simultaneously.

The evaluation was based on operating conditions from the ITS platform Nota AI deployed in 2025 across approximately 800 CCTV channels and 200 smart intersections in Daejeon, South Korea. The test covered the complete video analytics pipeline, including video decoding, vehicle and pedestrian detection, object tracking, video rendering and transmission of analyzed footage. This approach validated the integrated solution under conditions designed to reflect real-world video monitoring operations, rather than measuring AI model inference speed alone.

Nota Vision Agent combines computer vision and VLM technologies to analyze objects, actions and contextual events in real time. It also automatically summarizes key findings in reports, helping improve the efficiency of monitoring operations. Nota AI's model compression and hardware optimization technologies enable the solution to run efficiently across a range of computing environments, including servers, cloud infrastructure, mobile platforms and edge devices.

Nota AI and Intel plan to build on the launch through joint customer development, deployment consulting and on-site technical support. The companies also intend to expand the application of Nota AI's optimization technology across Intel hardware platforms and identify new opportunities in industrial AI markets, including intelligent transportation, industrial safety and selective video monitoring.

"This integrated solution brings together Nota AI's optimization expertise and Intel's hardware capabilities to deliver the performance required in real-world industrial environments," said Myungsu Chae, CEO of Nota AI. "The value of AI optimization lies in enabling AI to operate effectively across diverse industries. We will continue expanding customers' infrastructure options so they can deploy AI systems tailored to the requirements of each site."

"The results Nota AI is achieving with Intel Arc Pro B70 GPUs reflect the strength of a platform purpose-built for enterprise AI," said Michael Monson, Intel Arc Pro product manager. "Our Arc Pro B-series GPUs are designed to provide high-performance, cost-efficient AI compute for enterprises. We're excited to see Nota AI's customers benefit from the Vision Agent B70 optimizations, demonstrating the powerful potential of full-stack collaboration between Intel and its enterprise partners."
